audit.summary: Independent acceptance confirms all ten reported discrepancies. Problem P3 is Major because a false expansion occurs in the supplied proof of the central kernel identity and its downstream Bailey-tree use is explicit. The finite repair is demonstrated; the kernel and main conclusions are not disproved. Nine other findings remain Minor because the exact surviving arguments and local scopes are identified. Cited prior-kernel equivalences remain unverified from complete retained sources.

proposition.location:
Retained report, Problem 1: Problem 1 (Minor; p. 4, first unnumbered identity). The prefactor for the \(\tau=-1\) specialization has the wrong modulus.

Retained report, Problem 2: Problem 2 (Minor; p. 5, paragraph following Theorem 1.3). The highest-weight label omits the level shift by three.

Retained report, Problem 3: Problem 3 (Major; p. 17, proof of Theorem 4.2). The double sum immediately below the transformed \({}_2\phi_1\) loses a factor and has an incorrect exponent.

Retained report, Problem 4: Problem 4 (Minor; p. 30, first constant-term equality for \(A_{\nu;k}\)). An extra column-index term makes the first constant-term expression false.

Retained report, Problem 5: Problem 5 (Minor; p. 31, last display of the proof of Theorem 1.2). The final product sign repeats an already expanded three-factor theta product.

Retained report, Problem 6: Problem 6 (Minor; p. 32, parameter bounds preceding Theorem 6.1). Two primed-parameter bounds are misstated.

Retained report, Problem 7: Problem 7 (Minor; p. 32, first modulus-seven identity). The factor \((q^7;q^7)_\infty\) needs exponent two.

Retained report, Problem 8: Problem 8 (Minor; p. 37, equation (7.6)). The last index in the quadratic exponent must be \(j\).

Retained report, Problem 9: Problem 9 (Minor; p. 42, equation (8.10b)). The first argument of the subtracted character is \(z\), not \(q\).

Retained report, Problem 10: Problem 10 (Minor; p. 46, opening factorial identity). The base of each factor on the left must be \(q^r\).
